clue.text: A saint united like the early morning flower?

parts.note: the Venerable Bede, the Anglo-Saxon monk and historian, is a saint
joined in marriage means wed

explanation.surface: A holy man joined in wedlock is compared to a flower at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a flower at dawn is typically covered in dew.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers early in the day are wet with dew, so they are moistened in exactly this way.

clue.text: Loving, without discrimination, store supplying mulled wine

parts.note: bi, short for bisexual, describes loving either sex without discriminating
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: An indiscriminately affectionate shop sells hot spiced wine.
explanation.walkthrough: BISHOP is an old name for a hot drink of wine mulled with oranges and spices.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishop is a traditional English drink of port or red wine heated with spices and fruit.

clue.text: Famine departs this world

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
the earth is the world we live on

explanation.surface: Starvation causes someone to leave this life.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a severe scarcity, especially of food, which is what a famine is.

clue.text: Where's Devon without its capital? Bust, any old time

indicators.note: bust as broken signals that the letters are smashed and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: read as where is, both letters of the contraction count

indicators.note: the capital letter of Devon, its initial D, is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone asks where Devon has gone with its county town missing, and declares it ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without its capital' takes D from DEVON to leave EVON; 'Bust' then rearranges WHERES plus EVON. Exeter is Devon's county town, a decoy for 'capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whensoever is an emphatic form of whenever, meaning at whatever time at all.

clue.text: Founder member of the "Gang of Four" dropping ecstasy

indicators.note: dropping means the drug letter is let fall out of the politician's name

parts.note: Dr David Owen was one of the four Labour politicians who founded the SDP in 1981
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A founding figure of a famous political quartet gives up drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a noun tied to the Gang of Four but is the verb meaning sink. The Gang of Four broke from Labour to found the Social Democratic Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that founders fills with water and sinks, just as a person who drowns goes under.

clue.text: Report on way back, as ruled by head of religion

parts.note: a report is a bang, or pop

indicators.note: back tells us the word for way is read in reverse

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner

explanation.surface: A journalist files a story on a return journey about a church's spiritual leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is the noise of a gun, not a news story; 'back' reverses the word for way. Popedom names the Pope's realm, the domain ruled by him.
explanation.definitionFit: Popedom is the office and domain of the Pope, who rules as head of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Recruitment company (media sector) to go north of the border

parts.note: the press is the newspaper part of the media

parts.words: to go north of the border
parts.note: gang is the Scots word for go, used north of the English border

explanation.surface: A hiring firm in the newspaper business plans to relocate to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of the border' means in Scotland, where gang means go.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang was a body of men who forcibly enlisted sailors, an old means of recruitment.

clue.text: Have a go at drinking wine, primarily hock

indicators.note: drinking means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: to pan something is to criticise or have a go at it

indicators.note: primarily picks out the opening letter of wine

explanation.surface: Someone tries sampling wine, starting with a German white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hock' looks like the German wine but is the verb meaning to pledge for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: To hock something is slang for leaving it with a pawnbroker as security for money.

clue.text: Raised support along cracks running at angle

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: aid is help or support

indicators.note: cracks signals that the following word breaks apart and is rearranged

explanation.surface: Lifted props run along fissures set at a slant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns AID into DIA; 'cracks' rearranges ALONG into GONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal line slants across between opposite corners rather than running square.

clue.text: They look out for each other no better than bitchy types, it's said

definitions.text: They look out for each other

indicators.note: it's said signals that the words are spoken and heard as something else

parts.note: mere means no better than, and cats are spiteful, bitchy people

explanation.surface: A group who watch each other's backs are said to be just a bunch of catty gossips.
explanation.walkthrough: Meerkats famously post sentries who stand on their hind legs and watch for predators on behalf of the colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Meerkats live in colonies where lookouts keep watch for danger for the whole group.

clue.text: Drink — after second time, urinate

indicators.note: after means the drink comes later than the other two letters

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone needs the toilet after a second round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: STALE as a verb is used of horses and cattle passing water.
explanation.definitionFit: To stale is to pass urine, a term used chiefly of horses and other livestock.

clue.text: Quality of fishnet tights makes Frank get windy

parts.note: frank means candid or open
to weave is to wind or twist about, as a winding road does

explanation.surface: Fishnet stockings make a man called Frank nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name and 'windy' like nervous; they are OPEN and the verb WEAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishnet is a loose mesh with large holes, which is the very nature of an open-weave fabric.

clue.text: Output from quite useless boiler? Sense perverse, slow-witted quality

parts.note: a boiler's heat output is measured in BTUs, British thermal units, and a quite useless one gives 0 of them

indicators.note: perverse means twisted, so the word is turned into a different order

explanation.surface: A dud boiler puts out nothing, and a stubborn lack of sense is the dull result.
explanation.walkthrough: BTUs, British thermal units, measure heat output; a useless boiler produces 0 of them. 'perverse' rearranges SENSE into ENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuseness is slowness to understand, the condition of being dim or slow-witted.

clue.text: Jumper reduced at neck end — swindle!

parts.note: roo is a shortened kangaroo, a famous jumper

indicators.note: neck end means the final letter of the word neck

explanation.surface: A sweater is taken in at the collar, and the buyer feels cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a British sweater but is the kangaroo; 'reduced' clips it to its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat or swindle them, especially out of money.

clue.text: Play sailor who's blind drunk: "I can't act without a pint initially!"

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters are reeling into a new order
initially takes just the opening letter of pint

explanation.surface: An inebriated actor insists he cannot perform without a pint first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blind drunk' looks like one phrase, but 'blind' ends the definition and 'drunk' rearranges ICANTACT plus A and P. Captain Cat is the blind old sea captain in Dylan Thomas's play Under Milk Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The blind retired seaman who dreams of his drowned shipmates in Under Milk Wood.

clue.text: Lavish more on tramp? Not right

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: not right asks for the letter standing for right to be taken away

parts.note: a vagrant is a tramp

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to give more generously to a homeless man, and is told no.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish and extravagant both describe spending or giving far beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Sailor not fussed about cutting hair

indicators.note: fussed suggests agitation, so the letters are stirred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A seaman is unbothered about getting a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fussed' reads as relaxed, but 'fussed' rearranges SAILOR plus NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to barbers and their work of cutting hair.

clue.text: After second wicket, Bury tailender dismissed stroke-makers

indicators.note: after means the remaining piece follows the two abbreviations

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket

indicators.note: the tailender is the last letter, and dismissed sends it away

parts.note: to immerse something is to bury or plunge it

explanation.surface: In a cricket match, after the second wicket falls, the last batsman from Bury is out.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (wicket, tailender, a team from the town of Bury) hides IMMERSE losing its final E. Swimmers make strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimmers move through water using strokes such as crawl or breaststroke.

clue.text: Parking lot: wind-battered location of scientific hoax

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the two words' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car park battered by gales is the site of a famous fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges LOT plus WIND into ILTDOWN. Piltdown in Sussex is where the faked fossil Piltdown Man was 'found' in 1912.
explanation.definitionFit: Piltdown in East Sussex gave its name to Piltdown Man, a forged fossil exposed in 1953.

clue.text: Think about storing energy in island as a rescuer

indicators.note: in places the assembled letters inside the island's name

parts.note: the Isle of Wight lies off the south coast of England

indicators.note: storing means the rearranged word holds the energy letter
about suggests turning round, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A thinker considers holding some power on an island so as to come to the rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the word for think and 'storing' puts E inside to give HITEKN. In business a white knight rescues a firm from a hostile bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A white knight is a saviour, in finance a friendly bidder rescuing a company from takeover.

clue.text: Radio astronomer's strong feeling for lines

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the astronomer is the strong feeling plus lines

parts.note: love is a strong feeling

explanation.surface: A scientist's passion is for poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Bernard Lovell founded the Jodrell Bank radio telescope in Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bernard Lovell was a British pioneer of radio astronomy at Jodrell Bank.

clue.text: Absurdist playwright's timeless martyr

indicators.note: time-less asks for the letter for time to be removed

parts.note: Samuel Beckett wrote absurdist plays such as Waiting for Godot; the 's is is

explanation.surface: An absurdist dramatist's work is said to be an enduring sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' looks like eternal but means without T. Thomas Becket was the Archbishop of Canterbury murdered in his cathedral in 1170.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Becket was killed in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170 and venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Have sex with accent on tea

definitions.meaning: animals pair to breed, so to couple with
the South American herbal tea brewed from yerba leaves is spelt with an acute accent over its final letter

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the tea's spelling: the grid drops the accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to couple sexually; maté is a South American herbal infusion drunk as tea.

clue.text: Party politician's last vote round in utterly fanciful, would-be 18

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of politician's, ignoring the possessive
in puts the vote and the round inside the word for utterly

parts.note: quite means utterly or completely
X is the mark made on a ballot paper to vote
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: At a party a politician casts a final vote in a quite fantastical way.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is WHITE KNIGHT: Don Quixote is the fanciful would-be knight of Cervantes's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes's hero imagines himself a chivalrous knight rescuing ladies, a deluded would-be gallant.

clue.text: Unique, endlessly entertaining picture card

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A one-off, endlessly amusing illustrated postcard.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the queen is one of the three court or picture cards.

clue.text: Posing like deposed ruler

indicators.note: deposed means removed, so the word for like is taken out

parts.note: posing a question is asking it
as means like

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a pose like a monarch who has been overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposed ruler' looks like the definition; 'deposed' instead removes AS from ASKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male monarch, who rules over a kingdom.

clue.text: Coteries developed with one at the centre add stimulation

indicators.note: at the centre places the letter in the middle of the rearranged word
developed means the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Social cliques evolve with a single person at their heart, adding excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges COTERIES into EROTCISE; 'at the centre' puts I in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To eroticise something is to give it sexual excitement, adding a stimulating quality.

clue.text: Stop language broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the word is heard spoken

parts.note: Czech is the language of the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A radio station halts a foreign-language programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to halt or restrain it, as in checking an advance.

clue.text: Information about entering secure country

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to seal something is to secure it

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Data about entering a safe nation.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN, British slang for information, is turned round by 'about' to give NEG; the surface reads 'about' as concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African country on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: TV money-raiser rejected — Henry released informal communication

indicators.note: released means the letter is let go
rejected means thrown back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a telethon is a long television broadcast raising money for charity
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A TV charity appeal is turned down and Henry is let go, as a quick note explains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TELETHON into NOHTELET, and 'released' drops H.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for a short informal note or message.
